title: Welfare Schemes for Hill-Based Minority Communities implemented by  Ministry of Minority Affairs
body_text:
Ministry of Minority Affairs implements the following schemes/programmes for socio-economic empowerment of the six (6) centrally notified minority communities namely Buddhists, Christians, Jains, Muslims, Parsis and Sikhs across the country including the state of West Bengal irrespective of any topographic conditions:
1. PRADHAN MANTRI VIRASAT KA SAMVARDHAN (PM VIKAS)
The Ministry of Minority Affairs is implementing Pradhan Mantri Virasat Ka Samvardhan (PM VIKAS), an integrated Central Sector Scheme by combining the five erstwhile livelihood schemes, namely Seekho Aur Kamao, USTTAD, Hamari Dharohar, Nai Roshni and Nai Manzil, to facilitate opportunities for minority communities in education, skilling and employment. The Scheme comprises four components, namely (i) Skilling and Training, (ii) Women Leadership and Entrepreneurship, (iii) Education, and (iv) Infrastructure Development through convergence with Pradhan Mantri Jan Vikas Karyakram (PMJVK), wherever required.
2. PRADHAN MANTRI JAN VIKAS KARYAKRAM (PMJVK)
PMJVK, a Centrally Sponsored Scheme aims to create community infrastructure in Minority Concentration Areas across the country in sectors such as Health, Education, Skill Development, Women-centric Projects, Drinking Water and Sanitation, Sports, Renewable Energy and other community infrastructure.
3. CONCESSIONAL CREDIT SCHEMES OF NATIONAL MINORITIES DEVELOPMENT & FINANCE CORPORATION (NMDFC)
So far as NMDFC is concerned, it is functioning to promote the socio-economic development of the notified minority communities, namely Muslims, Christians, Sikhs, Buddhists, Parsis and Jains, across the country, including hill-based minority communities.
Under Credit Line-1 (CL-1) , persons having an annual family income of up to ₹3.00 lakh are eligible for financial assistance under NMDFC schemes. Under Credit Line-2 (CL-2) , persons having an annual family income of up to ₹8.00 lakh are eligible for financial assistance.
NMDFC implements its concessional credit schemes through State Channelising Agencies (SCAs) nominated by the respective State Governments/UT Administrations. In the State of West Bengal, the West Bengal Minorities Development & Finance Corporation (WBMDFC) is the designated State Channelising Agency and implements NMDFC schemes for eligible minority beneficiaries, including those belonging to hill-based minority communities, in accordance with the prescribed guidelines.
This information was given by Union Minister of Minority Affairs Shri Kiren Rijiju in a written reply in Rajya Sabha today.
***
AK/MR

enrichment.summary: In a written reply to the Rajya Sabha on 10 August 2026, Union Minister of Minority Affairs Kiren Rijiju detailed three key welfare mechanisms for India's six centrally notified minority communities (Buddhists, Christians, Jains, Muslims, Parsis, Sikhs), applicable nationwide including hill-based minority areas and West Bengal. These are the PM VIKAS scheme for education, skilling and employment; the PMJVK scheme for community infrastructure in minority concentration areas; and concessional credit schemes run by the National Minorities Development & Finance Corporation (NMDFC) through State Channelising Agencies such as the West Bengal Minorities Development & Finance Corporation.
enrichment.context:
Pradhan Mantri Virasat Ka Samvardhan (PM VIKAS) was launched as an integrated Central Sector Scheme by merging five earlier livelihood schemes — Seekho Aur Kamao, USTTAD, Hamari Dharohar, Nai Roshni, and Nai Manzil — reflecting a broader government trend of scheme rationalization to reduce overlap and improve delivery efficiency for minority welfare. It focuses on skilling, women's leadership and entrepreneurship, education, and infrastructure convergence with PMJVK. Pradhan Mantri Jan Vikas Karyakram (PMJVK), earlier known as the Multi-sectoral Development Programme (MsDP), is a Centrally Sponsored Scheme targeting Minority Concentration Areas with infrastructure in health, education, skilling, drinking water, sanitation, and renewable energy, aiming to address the developmental deficit highlighted by the Sachar Committee report on the socio-economic status of Muslims and other minorities.

NMDFC, a Section 8 company under the Ministry of Minority Affairs, extends concessional credit to economically weaker sections among minorities through State Channelising Agencies (SCAs), with income eligibility thresholds (₹3 lakh under Credit Line-1 and ₹8 lakh under Credit Line-2) designed to reach a broader base of beneficiaries, including women entrepreneurs and self-employed individuals. Such reply-based disclosures in Parliament are a recurring means by which the government provides updates on scheme implementation, coverage, and state-specific execution, which are relevant to tracking the effectiveness and reach of minority welfare architecture in India, an important theme for both governance and social justice components of the UPSC syllabus.

prelims_questions.question:
Pradhan Mantri Virasat Ka Samvardhan (PM VIKAS) scheme was formed by merging which of the following erstwhile schemes?
1. Seekho Aur Kamao
2. USTTAD
3. Nai Manzil
4. Stand-Up India
Select the correct answer using the code below:
prelims_questions.explanation: As per the release, PM VIKAS integrates five erstwhile schemes: Seekho Aur Kamao, USTTAD, Hamari Dharohar, Nai Roshni, and Nai Manzil. Stand-Up India is a separate scheme under the Ministry of Finance for SC/ST and women entrepreneurs, not part of PM VIKAS.

prelims_questions.question:
With reference to the National Minorities Development & Finance Corporation (NMDFC), consider the following statements:
1. It provides concessional credit only to Muslims and Christians among notified minorities.
2. Under Credit Line-2, families with annual income up to ₹8 lakh are eligible for assistance.
3. NMDFC schemes are implemented through State Channelising Agencies nominated by State Governments/UTs.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
prelims_questions.explanation: NMDFC covers all six notified minority communities (Buddhists, Christians, Jains, Muslims, Parsis, Sikhs), not just two, making statement 1 incorrect. Statements 2 and 3 are accurate as per the release: Credit Line-2 covers families with income up to ₹8 lakh, and schemes are implemented via State Channelising Agencies like WBMDFC in West Bengal.

mains_questions.question: Discuss the significance of scheme convergence and rationalization, as seen in the merger of multiple minority welfare schemes into Pradhan Mantri Virasat Ka Samvardhan (PM VIKAS), for improving governance efficiency and outcomes in social sector delivery.

Examine the role of institutional mechanisms like the National Minorities Development & Finance Corporation (NMDFC) in promoting financial inclusion among minority communities in India. What are the challenges in ensuring equitable access to such concessional credit schemes across states?
